item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip.
They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed with just nine games to go before October.
But perhaps taking priority over chasing playoff positioning, Roberts expressed confidence that the Dodgers could finish the season relatively healthy with both Shohei Ohtani and Blake Snell progressing well in the final two weeks of the regular season.
"I think it's about winning games, all the while ... getting our players back to health. But I think they can go hand in hand," Roberts said. "We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games and at the same time, making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts."
Ohtani, who has been rehabbing at home while the Dodgers were on the road, swung a bat for the second time since landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 8. The two-way superstar took another step forward in his hitting progression as he took batting practice off of coach pitch and came away feeling good, per Roberts. While the Dodgers' skipper acknowledged "he's not there yet" as far as facing live pitching, that would be the next hurdle for Ohtani to clear before returning to the lineup.
In an ideal world, Roberts said he'd like for Ohtani to take somewhere around 10-12 at-bats in live batting practice before he gets activated, but acknowledged that it's really dependent on Ohtani himself.
"It's been a really productive three-to-four-to-five days. He's in a good spot," Roberts said. "No matter what I say, it really doesn't matter in the sense of it's what he feels good with, what gets him ready."
Snell, who exited his last start in Cincinnati after pitching just one inning with left groin tightness, continues to feel good and the overall sense is that he avoided a serious injury. Snell threw 90 feet on Friday while wearing a wrap around his left groin area, and Roberts is "very hopeful" that the former Cy Young winner can make one more regular season start.
Roberts is not sure when exactly that would be but did say that it would be a full start to ramp Snell up for the postseason rather than an abbreviated one.
"It'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said. "But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."
The Dodgers' depleted bullpen does get some reinforcements back with closer Edwin Díaz being activated from the IL. He's available to pitch on Friday night if needed, and Roberts didn't rule out using him in low leverage situations to try and get him into a rhythm ahead of October.
Roberts also said that he expects outfielder Andy Pages to be activated at some point in the final home series against the San Diego Padres and catcher Dalton Rushing has also been progressing well, though there's no timeline on his return just yet.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Two days after he exited a start following just one inning due to left groin tightness, Blake Snell threw from 90 feet on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants. He emerged feeling good, with the Dodgers believing they avoided the worst with an injury that’s been a recurring issue throughout the left-hander’s career.
“Happy that we caught it early,” said manager Dave Roberts, who noted that Snell was not sent to receive any imaging.
The Dodgers remain optimistic that the two-time Cy Young Award winner will make another regular-season start sometime during their remaining nine games. The specific day is to be determined -- his regular spot in the rotation would come up during L.A.’s three-game series vs. San Diego that begins on Tuesday -- but he is not expected to pitch with any limitations.
“I think it'd be more of a normal start,” said Roberts. “Maybe not pushing him a ton, given that we don't know how the season's going to play out. But this will be his last regular-season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start.”
Snell began the season on the 15-day injured list with left shoulder fatigue, not making his season debut until May 9. He almost immediately went back on the IL due to loose bodies in his left elbow, which were removed using the NanoNeedle Scope procedure. Since returning on Aug. 11, Snell has looked like he hasn’t missed a beat, pitching to a 1.01 ERA over seven starts, with 47 strikeouts and 14 walks in 35 2/3 innings.
For a pitcher who shares a rotation with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal, Snell is an absolutely vital part of the Dodgers’ postseason rotation plans. Should his condition worsen, the Dodgers’ starting pitching depth suddenly looks pretty thin. There’s Tyler Glasnow, who started on Friday against San Francisco but has dealt with injury issues of his own this year. Roki Sasaki (out since Aug. 27 with a right middle finger blister) is also expected to return soon for one final regular-season start.
Given Snell’s history of pitching well following long layoffs from Major League action, have the Dodgers given any consideration to letting him skip his next start, continuing to rest and waiting to have him pitch again once postseason games get underway?
“There is a thought,” said Roberts. “But you're still talking about a potential 17 days, something like that -- that's a long time to not be in competition. Where typically, with his history, you still have rehabs and things like that. So it's just not kind of a plug-and-play, sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game.”

item.title: [MLB.com] Ohtani sigue dando pasos para regresar antes del final de la temporada regular
item.dc:creator: Sarah Wexler
item.description: LOS ÁNGELES -- Mientras Shohei Ohtani avanza en su recuperación de lesiones en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho, los Dodgers reafirmaron que sigue encaminado a regresar antes de que termine la temporada regular. El viernes dio el siguiente paso hacia ese objetivo, cuando tomó práctica de bateo ante lanzamientos de un coach. “Salió bien de la sesión”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Creo que, por mi parte, simplemente estoy esperando saber cuándo va a salir al terreno, ni hablar de tomar p
item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Mientras Shohei Ohtani avanza en su recuperación de lesiones en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho, los Dodgers reafirmaron que sigue encaminado a regresar antes de que termine la temporada regular. El viernes dio el siguiente paso hacia ese objetivo, cuando tomó práctica de bateo ante lanzamientos de un coach.
“Salió bien de la sesión”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Creo que, por mi parte, simplemente estoy esperando saber cuándo va a salir al terreno, ni hablar de tomar práctica de bateo en vivo o enfrentar a Trajekt. Y todavía no ha llegado a ese punto. Pero por todo lo que he escuchado, han sido tres, cuatro o cinco días realmente productivos. Está en un buen momento”.
Ohtani está aumentando su carga de trabajo exclusivamente como bateador, ya que no se espera que vuelva a lanzar esta temporada, luego de su última presentación en la lomita el 3 de julio. Su estadía en la lista de lesionados de 15 días es retroactiva al 8 de septiembre, por lo que podría ser activado, como muy pronto, el miércoles. Eso le daría un máximo de cinco juegos para recuperar el ritmo ante pitcheo de Grandes Ligas antes del inicio de la postemporada.
A los Dodgers les ha ido bastante bien sin Ohtani, con marca de 6-3 y 48 carreras anotadas, para un promedio de 5.3 por juego, aunque todos esos encuentros fueron contra equipos fuera de la contienda. Por supuesto, su alineación está en su mejor versión con el cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso como primer bate... siempre y cuando esté saludable.
Durante buena parte de la temporada, Ohtani volvió a registrar números dignos del JMV, incluso mientras lidiaba con una serie de lesiones. Bateó .296 con 26 jonrones y OPS de .952 en sus primeros 110 juegos. Pero en los siguientes 24 encuentros antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados, bateó .198 (de 96-19), con OPS de .690 y 34 ponches, un tramo que coincidió con un intento de aumentar progresivamente su carga de trabajo como lanzador.
Finalmente, los Dodgers decidieron que su estrella de dos vías no sólo necesitaba concentrarse exclusivamente en batear, sino que lo mejor para todos los involucrados era que Ohtani se tomara un tiempo para permitir que su cuerpo descansara y se recuperara, en lugar de intentar seguir jugando pese a las molestias.
Como Ohtani permaneció en Los Ángeles trabajando en su recuperación durante la gira más reciente de los Dodgers, no pudo celebrar con sus compañeros el jueves después de que aseguraran su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas. Eso significa que tendrá que esperar hasta que el equipo asegure otro objetivo para poder descorchar la champaña.
“Ya hicimos eso, así que vamos a ganar hoy y volveremos a brindar con ellos más adelante”, dijo Roberts. “Pero no, no voy a hacer un brindis especial, porque también hay muchos otros jugadores que fueron parte de esto”.

item.dc:creator: Sarah Wexler
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- As Shohei Ohtani works his way back from left knee and right biceps injuries, the Dodgers affirmed that he remains on pace to return before the regular season ends. And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- As Shohei Ohtani works his way back from left knee and right biceps injuries, the Dodgers affirmed that he remains on pace to return before the regular season ends. His next step toward that goal came on Friday, when Ohtani hit coach-pitch batting practice.
“He came out of it well,” said manager Dave Roberts. “I think for me, I'm just really waiting to hear when he's going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt. And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot.”
Ohtani is building up exclusively as a hitter, as he is not expected to pitch again this season, having last appeared on the mound on July 3. His 15-day injured list stint is backdated to Sept. 8, so the earliest he can be activated is Wednesday -- giving him, at most, five games to find his footing against Major League pitching before the postseason gets underway.
The Dodgers have fared well enough with Ohtani out, going 6-3 while scoring 48 runs, good for 5.3 runs per game (albeit exclusively against non-contending teams). Of course, their lineup is at its best with the four-time MVP hitting leadoff … provided that he’s healthy.
For most of the season, Ohtani was once again putting up MVP-caliber numbers, even as he battled a spate of injuries, batting .296 with 26 homers and a .952 OPS through his first 110 games. But over the next 24 games ahead of landing on the IL, he hit .198 (19-for-96) with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts, a stretch coinciding with an attempted pitching ramp-up.
Ultimately, the Dodgers decided that their two-way star needed not only to focus exclusively on hitting, but that the best thing for everyone involved was Ohtani taking some time to let his body rest and recover rather than trying to continue to play through it.
Since Ohtani remained in L.A. to work on his recovery during the Dodgers’ most recent road trip, he missed out on celebrating with his teammates on Thursday after they clinched their 13th NL West title in the past 14 seasons. That means he’ll have to wait for another clinch in order to pop some champagne.
“We already did that, so we're gonna win today, and we'll re-toast with them going forward,” said Roberts. “But no, I'm not going to do a special toast, because there's a lot of other players that were part of this, too.”

item.content:encoded:
MARLINS (AP) — Kyle Tucker conectó el sexto grand slam de su carrera y se quedó a un doble de completar el ciclo por los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, quienes vencieron el viernes 6-2 a los Marlins de Miami para ampliar a ocho triunfos su mejor racha de la temporada.
Tucker conectó un sweeper en cuenta de 1-1 del relevista Cade Gibson para poner la pizarra 6-1 en el séptimo inning. Pegó un sencillo en el primero y un triple en el sexto.
Max Muncy totalizó tres hits y una base por bolas, y Will Smith añadió un sencillo impulsor de carrera por los Dodgers, líderes de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Blake Snell (4-1) permitió una carrera y ponchó a ocho durante cinco innings y dos tercios, en los que toleró cuatro inatrapables.
Después de que los Dodgers tomaron una ventaja de 2-0 con el sencillo impulsor de Smith, el dominicano Agustín Ramírez conectó un doble impulsor que recortó la diferencia a 2-1. Victor Vodnik abrió el séptimo retirando rápidamente a Alex Freeland y al boricua Kiké Hernández, pero dio bases por bolas a Tommy Edman y Mookie Betts y permitió un sencillo de Muncy para llenar las bases, preparando el batazo de Tucker entre el jardín derecho y el central ante Gibson.
El dominicano Otto López conectó cuatro hits y el venezolano Javier Sanoja conectó un triple y un sencillo por los Marlins, que han perdido siete de ocho y cuatro seguidos. El abridor Ryan Gusto (1-5) permitió dos carreras con cinco hits.
El derecho otorgó tres bases por bolas y ponchó a tres.
Deportes AP: https://apnews.com/hub/deportes

The San Francisco Giants begin a three-game road series against the Los Angeles Dodgers tonight. Just a heads up that this is yet another Apple TV broadcast only.
Taking the mound for the Giants will be left-hander Cesar Perdomo, who enters tonight’s game with a 3.68 ERA, 4.19 FIP, with 11 strikeouts to four walks in 14.2 innings pitched. His last start was in the Giants’ 7-6 loss to the San Diego Padres last Saturday, in which he allowed five runs on 10 hits with three strikeouts and two walks in four and two thirds innings.
He’ll be facing off against Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow, who enters tonight’s game with a 3.50 ERA, 2.93 FIP, with 77 strikeouts to 21 walks in 61.2 innings pitched. His last start was in the Dodgers’ 4-3 win over the Miami Marlins on Saturday, in which he allowed four runs on five hits with seven strikeouts and four walks in four innings.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers hopeful to avoid worst-case scenario with injured star pitcher
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season. Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he wa
item.content:encoded:
So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season.
Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he was "very hopeful" in the left-hander's chances to get back on the mound before the beginning of the playoffs.
"Happy that we caught it early," Roberts said of Snell's injury.
Indeed, when Snell exited Wednesday's game after 19 pitches, it raised immediate concerns about the state of the Dodgers' rotation.
Given the injuries the team is dealing with in its bullpen and its offense's inconsistent form through the second half of the season, the Dodgers will almost certainly need to lean on their starters during the playoffs — similar to the way they did last year, when a rotation of Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Shohei Ohtani (who will effectively be replaced by Tarik Skubal this year) carried the pitching staff to a second consecutive World Series title.
Losing Snell — who was already sidelined for three months earlier this season following an elbow procedure and has a history of left groin injuries throughout his career — would have dealt a massive blow to those plans.
However, the Dodgers are at least initially optimistic they've avoided anything close to a worst-case scenario.
While Roberts acknowledged that there is still "a little bit of uncertainty" regarding Snell, and no exact date for when he might pitch again, the skipper also noted that the two-time Cy Young Award winner didn't require medical imaging; another sign of the team's confidence that his injury was not more severe.
It's possible that, even if Snell continues to feel better, the Dodgers could elect to rest him for the remainder of the regular season to ensure he doesn't suffer any further setbacks before the playoffs.
But, they are also wary of giving Snell too long of a layoff entering the postseason.
"It's not just kind of plug-and-play," Roberts said, "[to] sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game."
Thus, the team will continue to monitor Snell's progress in the coming days, hopeful that a potential pitching crisis has been averted.
"We feel confident," Roberts said.

RESUMEN
EL NUEVO DIARIO, LOS ÁNGELES.- El cerrador de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Edwin Díaz, salió el viernes de la lista de lesionados tras perderse un mes de actividad debido a una lesión en el cuello, según un reporte de MLB.com.
El lanzador derecho de 32 años estuvo disponible en el bullpen para el inicio de la serie contra San Francisco.
Díaz registra una marca de 2-2 y una efectividad de 11.85 en 16 partidos con los Dodgers. Firmó con el equipo como agente libre durante la pasada temporada baja.
Realizó cinco apariciones de rehabilitación durante su segunda estancia en la lista de lesionados esta temporada. Díaz permitió seis carreras y logró cuatro ponches en 4 entradas y un tercio.
El lanzador derecho Landon Knack fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City, un día después de lanzar cuatro entradas en blanco en una victoria sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati.

item.content:encoded:
Díaz podría lanzar entradas de baja presión mientras lucha por un puesto en playoffs
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES - Los Dodgers firmaron al puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz la temporada baja pasada con la firme intención de que fuera su cerrador para el 2026 y más allá. Ahora que regresa tras su segunda estancia en la lista de lesionados esta temporada, se ve obligado a luchar por un puesto en el bullpen de L.A. para la postemporada.
Antes del inicio de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes en el Dodger Stadium, los Dodgers activaron a Díaz de la lista de lesionados de 15 días, a la que había ingresado el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Como movimiento correspondiente, el lanzador derecho Landon Knack fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ha sido un año turbulento para Díaz, quien el 12 de diciembre firmó un contrato de tres años y $US69 millones con los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial. Huelga decir que las cosas no han salido según lo previsto para el tres veces seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas. En sus primeras siete presentaciones, permitió siete carreras limpias en seis entradas, con 10 ponches y cinco bases por bolas; posteriormente, ingresó a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en el codo derecho que requirieron cirugía.
Tras su regreso el 29 de julio, Díaz retomó el rol de cerrador, aunque esta vez registró tres oportunidades de salvamento desperdiciadas en nueve partidos y acumuló una efectividad de 12.91, con nueve ponches, cinco bases por bolas y dos bateadores golpeados en 7 entradas y 2/3 de labor.
La asignación de rehabilitación más reciente de Díaz no generó mucha confianza. Aunque los resultados eran menos importantes que sus sensaciones físicas, tuvo problemas de control: otorgó siete bases por bolas y golpeó a un bateador en cuatro entradas y 1/3 repartidas en cinco salidas con Oklahoma City, logrando además muy pocos swings fallidos.
Entonces, ¿qué debe hacer Díaz para demostrar que merece formar parte de los planes de L.A. para la postemporada?
"Creo que simplemente lanzar bien", dijo el manager Dave Roberts. "Para mí, el rol no importa. Creo que solo queremos verlo lanzar como él es capaz de hacerlo. Y estamos hablando de nueve partidos [restantes en la temporada regular], así que hablamos de tres o cuatro salidas para evaluar, y eso debería ser suficiente".
En este momento, ese rol no será el de "cerrador". Cabe esperar que Díaz sea utilizado en situaciones de menor presión. Tras asegurar su 13er título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas —y mientras luchan por obtener el pase directo a la segunda ronda de los playoffs—, los Dodgers tienen el lujo de aprovechar el resto del calendario de la temporada regular para que varios jugadores se ganen, en la práctica, un puesto en el roster de octubre.
Díaz podría ser la figura más destacada de ese grupo. Este tres veces ganador del premio al Relevista del Año podría convertirse en un factor clave en el bullpen de Los Ángeles en su búsqueda de un tercer título consecutivo, siempre y cuando demuestre ser una opción viable.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers could be getting one of their All-Stars back from injury. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told Dodger Insider that Andy Pages will return when the club hosts the San Diego Padres.
It had been previously reported that Pages would return on the Dodgers’ final homestand of the 2026 season. This update gives a firmer timeline for when the 2026 All-Star will return to the lineup.
Pages has been a huge boost to the Dodgers’ lineup. The 25-year-old has slashed .272/.358/.458 with 21 home runs and a 119 wRC+ in 127 games this season. He also provides elite center field defense, rated at +18 Defensive Runs Saved and +9 Outs Above Average.
Dodgers Provide Andy Pages Return Timeline
With a return date set for Andy Pages, that means he’ll get roughly six games of action to prepare for the postseason. Ideally, the Dodgers center fielder can shake off a month’s worth of rust, since he won’t have the luxury of a rehab assignment.
Pages suffered a fracture of his left hand when he got hit by a 100 MPH fastball from the Pirates‘ Bubba Chandler. The club has turned to Alek Thomas and Tommy Edman in center field in his absence.
Edman is currently penciled in as the everyday center fielder after Thomas struggled in a short stint. The former Diamondback was later DFA’d, then outrighted to Triple-A after seven games in the lineup.
With Pages returning, the Dodgers have some tough lineup decisions. Edman will most likely return to the infield, bumping Alex Freeland off second base and off the roster. With Teoscar Hernandez on a hot streak, the club is unlikely to take him out of the lineup.
Dodgers Right Now
At 93-60, the Dodgers are currently up four games in the loss column over the Atlanta Braves, meaning they’re in great position to earn a bye for the Wild Card round.
They’ve already taken care of the first step by securing their fifth straight National League West division title. Now it’s just setting themselves up for the best chance to make a run in the postseason.
There are a lot of injuries the club needs to navigate. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki, and Edgardo Henriquez are the big ones to follow. Getting Ohtani back and healthy is going to be important if the Dodgers want to finish their three-peat bid.
Los Angeles will finish their 2026 season in California. They host the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres on their final homestand. Then they’ll finish out the year in San Francisco.
The Dodgers will send right-hander Tyler Glasnow for the series opener against the Giants. First pitch at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium is set for 7:15 p.m. PT, with the game being broadcast on Apple TV+.

item.content:encoded:
ドジャースージャイアンツ（18日、ロサンゼルス）「右手中指のまめ」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている米大リーグ、ドジャースの佐々木朗希投手（24）が先発として実戦復帰間近であることが明らかとなった。試合前に取材に応じたデーブ・ロバーツ監督（54）が右腕の状態について語った。
「朗希は良い状態にあるし、投げたがっている。近いうちに復帰できると思う。日付は未定だけど、再び先発として投げることになるでしょう」
16日（日本時間17日）にIL入り後2度目となるライブBP（実戦形式の打撃練習）に登板し、4回を投げて50球を消化するなど復帰に向けて順調にステップを踏んでいる。
一方でチームの先発陣はポストシーズンに向け、不安要素を抱えている。16日のレッズ戦に先発したスネルが左股関節の張りを訴え、1回19球で緊急降板。万全な状態でポストシーズンを迎えることができるか不透明な中、復帰間近の佐々木が重要な存在になりそうだ。
指揮官は「防げるのであれば、先発陣の枚数が不足する事態は避けたい。だからこそ、朗希には4、5イニング程度を投げられるスタミナを維持させておく必要がある」と期待を寄せ、「状況に応じて役割を移行できる選択肢を残しておきたい」と先発でも救援でも起用が可能な24歳を〝ジョーカー〟としてスタンバイさせていく考えを示した。

item.title: [MLB.com] Díaz likely to pitch low-leverage innings as he vies for postseason spot
item.dc:creator: Sarah Wexler
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers signed Edwin Díaz last offseason with every intention of him being their closer, for 2026 and beyond. As he returns from his second injured list stint this season, he finds himself needing to fight for a role in L.A.’s postseason bullpen. Prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers activated Díaz from the 15-day IL, where he’d landed on Aug. 18 with neck inflammation. Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers signed Edwin Díaz last offseason with every intention of him being their closer, for 2026 and beyond. As he returns from his second injured list stint this season, he finds himself needing to fight for a role in L.A.’s postseason bullpen.
Prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers activated Díaz from the 15-day IL, where he’d landed on Aug. 18 with neck inflammation. Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City as the corresponding move.
It’s been a tumultuous year for Díaz, who on Dec. 12 signed a three-year, $69 million contract with the two-time reigning World Series champs. Needless to say, things have not gone as expected for the three-time All-Star. Across his first seven appearances, he allowed seven earned runs in six innings with 10 strikeouts and five walks, after which he landed on the IL with loose bodies in his right elbow that necessitated surgery.
Upon his return on July 29, Díaz slotted back into the closer role, this time recording three blown saves over nine games and pitching to a 12.91 ERA, with nine strikeouts, five walks and two hit batters in 7 2/3 innings pitched.
Díaz’s most recent rehab assignment didn’t do much to inspire confidence. Although the results were less important than how he came out feeling, he struggled with his command, issuing seven walks and hitting a batter in 4 1/3 innings across five appearances with Oklahoma City while recording very few swings and misses.
So what does Díaz have to do to prove he deserves to be part of L.A.’s postseason plans?
“I think just pitch well,” said manager Dave Roberts. “For me, it's regardless of the role. I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he's capable of. And you're talking about nine games [remaining in the regular season], so you're talking three or four outings to evaluate, and that should be adequate.”
At this point, that role will not be “closer.” Expect to see Díaz used in lower-leverage spots. With their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons now clinched -- even as they vie for a first-round bye -- the Dodgers have the luxury of being able to use their remaining regular-season slate to let a handful of guys essentially try out for October roster spots.
Díaz might just be the headliner of that group, as the three-time Reliever of the Year could prove to be an X-factor out of L.A.’s ’pen as it seeks a three-peat -- so long as he shows he’s a viable option.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are beginning their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have just nine more games in the regular season. After clinching the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years, they're still battling for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves.
If the Dodgers clinch one of the top two seeds, they'll secure a first-round bye. That is especially crucial this season as the team deals with injuries to a handful of key players.
Here's the latest updates on six of those players.
Shohei Ohtani Injury Update
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Friday that Ohtani is continuing to progress in his swinging progression.
“Everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three, four, five days," Roberts said. "He’s in a good spot.”
Ohtani has not yet progressed to hitting in live batting practice or off the Trajekt machine. Thus, a return doesn't appear to be imminent.
Ohtani is eligible to return on Wednesday, just five days before the final day of the regular season.
Blake Snell Injury Update
Snell gave the Dodgers a major scare when he exited his Wednesday start after one inning with left groin tightness.
Fortunately, Snell said the exit was more precautionary than anything, as he didn't want to make it worse by staying in the game.
Snell expressed optimism he'd be able to make another start before the end of the regular season. On Friday, Roberts struck a similar tone, saying he was "more confident" the left-hander would be able to make a normal start sometime next week in his regular season finale.
Snell didn't undergo imaging on his groin.
Andy Pages Injury Update
Pages has been out since Aug. 21 when he suffered a fractured hand that forced him to undergo surgery.
However, he rejoined the team at home on Friday, and is expected to be activated at some point during the homestand that goes through Thursday.
Pages told David Vassegh of AM570 that he's hoping to be activated by Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing Injury Update
Rushing told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic that he had a PRP injection to address his elbow injury that forced him to go back on the IL in early September.
The catcher remains hopeful he'll be able to return as a pinch-hit option off the bench for the postseason, but will know more after hitting off a machine in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki Injury Update
Sasaki threw four simulated innings this week and is expected to start "soon," per Roberts.
The team initially planned to move Sasaki to the bullpen, but will instead keep him stretched out as a starter as an insurance option.
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez surprisingly went on the IL with a low-grade back strain this past week, ending his regular season.
The Dodgers remain "hopeful" he'll be able to return in the postseason, per Roberts.

He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages is set to return on Tuesday against the San Diego Padres after missing a month with a hand fracture.
Pages suffered a fracture in his left hand on August 22nd in a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates. A pitch hit his hand, causing the injury.
The Cuban had surgery on his broken hand shortly after, and he has since steadily increased his baseball activity.
When will Andy Pages return?
On Friday, September 18th, before the Dodgers’ home game against the Giants, Pages told AM 570’s David Vassegh he hopes to return for Tuesday’s game against the Padres.
Manager Dave Roberts has already told the media, including Dodgers Nation, that Pages would be activated at some point during the homestand.
The Dodgers will be home from Friday to Wednesday, before ending their regular season against the Giants in San Francisco.
If Pages does return on Tuesday, that would give him five games to get up to MLB game speed.
Assuming he rests one of those, Pages would have only four games to get everything clicking.
Why the Dodgers need Andy Pages back
Pages is an elite defender, with a 9.5 defensive rating, according to FanGraphs.
Tommy Edman, who has taken on the center field responsibilities, has -1 outs above average. While Pages has 8 outs above average at center field, according to Baseball Savant.
For a team that prides itself on defense, Pages presents the glove and range needed to help keep runs down and help the starting pitching stay in the game.
Pages has a 3.9 fWAR and a 119 wRC+ this season, and as a hitter, he brings a good bat-on-ball skill set.
On both ends of the field, Pages is invaluable to the Dodgers, and they will need him for the postseason.

I approach this matchup strictly from a betting perspective. Los Angeles enters as a heavy home favorite, backed by a potent lineup and an elite starting arm in Tyler Glasnow. San Francisco looks overmatched as the road underdog, deploying a decimated roster against a superior opponent.

At 56 cents per contract on Polymarket, I am laying the runline with the home favorites. The Dodgers boast a 3.64 team ERA compared to San Francisco’s 4.35 mark. The pitching discrepancy alone justifies this position. Tyler Glasnow features a dominant 0.97 WHIP and an exceptional 11.24 strikeouts per nine innings. He should easily carve up a struggling Giants lineup.

Best Player Prop: Glasnow Over 6.5 Ks (-137 at Kalshi)
Glasnow possesses elite swing-and-miss stuff. Averaging 11.24 K/9, he clears this number with ease during a standard five-inning outing. BetMGM offers the best price on this prop.
Giants vs Dodgers Odds & Public Betting
The traditional betting market heavily favors the home team. Early splits show staggering support for Los Angeles. They command 95.6% of the moneyline tickets and 93.2% of the overall financial stake.
San Francisco draws virtually zero action as the road underdog. Bettors see no value in backing a struggling squad against an elite arm. You can view wider market consensus by checking the MLB public betting trends before first pitch.
The total runs market displays a similar consensus. The Over pulls in 86.5% of tickets and 87.2% of the total handle. Serious bettors expect the Dodgers to inflict heavy damage against an overmatched pitching staff.
Giants vs Dodgers Pitching Matchup
The Giants vs Dodgers pitching matchup is Cesar Perdomo vs Tyler Glasnow. These are two pitchers who have been trending in opposite directions lately.
This pitching duel presents a massive imbalance. Glasnow brings an electric arsenal, evidenced by his 2.93 FIP and microscopic 0.97 WHIP. He routinely limits hard contact while generating premium whiff rates. Over his last 55.2 innings and 10 starts, he maintained an 11.5 K/9 ratio.
Perdomo relies heavily on pitching to contact, generating just 5.91 K/9. That strategy spells disaster against a lineup capable of punishing mistakes. His 1.36 WHIP indicates he allows too many free passes and base hits, which creates high-leverage situations early in games.

Los Angeles owns superior season-long metrics across the board. They strike the ball harder, posting an 89.4 mph average exit velocity at home. Their pitching staff limits baserunners effectively, yielding a stellar 1.16 WHIP.
San Francisco frequently struggles to strand runners. Their 4.35 overall ERA highlights a persistent inability to escape jams. Checking MLB starting lineups reveals exactly how outmatched the Giants look on paper tonight.

Giants vs Dodgers Injury Report & Weather Impact
San Francisco attempts to compete without a functional starting infield. Missing Rafael Devers and Matt Chapman evaporates their offensive ceiling. Relying on replacement-level bats against an elite strikeout arm is a losing proposition.
Los Angeles navigates the loss of Shohei Ohtani smoothly thanks to stars like Mookie Betts. Their depth prevents major downgrades to their overall team projections.

Glasnow only provided four inning as well.
Heading into such a key stretch with the postseason around the corner, Glasnow has the chance to ease any doubts over his ability to deliver a quality playoff start.
With Blake Snell injured and facing an uncertain timeline, there is more riding on Glasnow than ever.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the Dodgers return to Los Angeles for a six-game homestand, which includes this series against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers just secured their fifth consecutive NL West crown on Thursday with a win over the Reds.
But there is still more baseball to be played before the postseason starts, and Los Angeles will be fighting for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers, who currently hold a two-game lead for the top seed in the NL.
If the Dodgers want to cut into Milwaukee’s lead, however, they will need to do so without superstar Shohei Ohtani, who remains on the injured list while recovering from several minor issues.
Fortunately, Ohtani is expected to return before the end of the regular season, but the Dodgers will need Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and the rest of the lineup to carry the offense against San Francisco.
Tyler Glasnow will get the start for Los Angeles tonight after posting a strong 4-1 record and 3.50 ERA this season, while San Francisco will counter with left-hander Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68 ERA).
The stakes of this rivalry matchup would normally be higher, but with the Giants well outside of the playoff picture, their only real motivation is trying to complicate Los Angeles’ final stretch before the postseason.

Watch Giants vs. Dodgers for free

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers begin their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers (93-60) clinched the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years on Thursday. The Giants (64-89) are a whopping 29 games behind LA in the division.
“It’s a big deal. It’s not easy,” manager Dave Roberts said of his team winning another NL West title. “I think a lot of people think it’s easy, it’s a rite of passage. But it’s not easy to win a division when everyone is gunning for you, to keep everyone motivated to play over the course of 162. It’s something we’re all really proud of. But that’s not the end goal.”
The Dodgers and Giants play six times over the next 10 days to close out the season. The Dodgers are just 3-4 against the Giants this season.
Dodgers vs Giants Pitching Matchup on Friday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the ball for the Dodgers on Friday night amid a concerning stretch of play.
The right-hander has allowed four runs in each of his last two starts. After his most recent one, manager Dave Roberts somewhat ominously said Glasnow "didn’t feel great" going into it.
Glasnow has made four starts since coming off the IL after a four-month absence due to a back injury. He left the team to go home early this week instead of traveling with them to Cincinnati as the staff wanted to have him avoid going on two flights.
The Dodgers will hope for better results from him on Friday, especially after Blake Snell left his Wednesday start with a groin injury.
For what it's worth, Glasnow's best start of the season came against the Giants in April, when he allowed one hit over eight shutout innings with nine strikeouts.
Opposite Glasnow will be left-hander Cesar Perdomo, who owns a 3.68 ERA over 14.2 career innings at the MLB level.
He made his debut on Sept. 1 as a reliever before starting each of his last two games.
Dodgers Lineup vs Giants
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Will Smith, C
- Teoscar Hernández, LF
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Miguel Rojas, 2B
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Kiké Hernández, 3B
- Alex Call, CF
- Josue De Paula, DH
Max Muncy and Alex Freeland are out of the lineup with the left-handed pitcher on the mound. Tommy Edman is also out.
How to Watch Dodgers vs Giants on Friday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Francisco Giants on Friday, Sept. 18 is 7:15 p.m. PT/10:15 p.m. ET.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have officially activated Edwin Diaz from the injured list and optioned reliever Landon Knack back down to the minor leagues.
Diaz has been rehabilitating down in Triple-A with the Oklahoma City Comets as he tries to recover from neck inflammation.
In 4.1 innings of work in the minors during his latest assignment, he has a 12.46 ERA.
With the season winding down for the Comets and Diaz still needing to pitch and prove that he can get outs, the Dodgers are giving him a shot on the major league roster.
Manager Dave Roberts has made it clear that Diaz needs to show tangible results in the regular season to get any standing in the bullpen trust tree.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said.
“So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
This story will be updated.

item.description: The Dodgers on Friday activated Edwin Díaz off the injured list, with a week and a half remaining in the regular season to see if his slim chance of pitching his way onto the postseason roster comes to fruition. Díaz, who signed a three-year contract with the Dodgers in December, struggled to open the season before undergoing arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April, which cost him three and a half months. In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers on Friday activated Edwin Díaz off the injured list, with a week and a half remaining in the regular season to see if his slim chance of pitching his way onto the postseason roster comes to fruition.
Díaz, who signed a three-year contract with the Dodgers in December, struggled to open the season before undergoing arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April, which cost him three and a half months.
In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has allowed runs in nine of them, with an 11.85 ERA, 6.37 xERA, 19 strikeouts and 10 walks in 13 2/3 innings. In nine games after returning from elbow surgery, Díaz had a 19.6-percent strikeout rate, down from 30.3 percent in seven games before surgery, and well below his 39.9-percent career strikeout rate through 2025.
The latest malady for Díaz was neck inflammation, sidelined since August 18. His rehab assignment with Oklahoma City didn't go well at all, throwing more balls than strikes in three of his five appearances, with six runs allowed in 4 1/3 innings, seven walks, and four strikeouts. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday in Cincinnati that Díaz will need to throw more strikes, and quality ones at that, in order to be considered to pitch in October.
"Like anything, it should be a meritocracy. You have to earn the right of opportunities, and you've also got to perform. Eddie understands that," Roberts said, as shown on SportsNet LA. "Where we're at now, we need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That's what he's about."
Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, after fulfilling his role with aplomb on Thursday. Called up for a day, Knack tossed four scoreless innings in relief and earned the win in the Dodgers' division clincher in Cincinnati.
In Knack's three stints in the majors this year, he pitched in four of the eight games for which he was active, with a 3.86 ERA and 4.09 xERA in build relief, with eight strikeouts and two walks in his 11 2/3 innings, plus one save of 2 2/3 innings, the Dodgers' longest save of the season.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Demote Pitcher, Officially Activate Edwin Diaz Amid Disastrous Season
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are giving Edwin Díaz one final chance to prove he belongs on the postseason roster. On Friday, ahead of their series opener against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers have officially activated Díaz off the 15-day injured list. In order to make room on the active roster, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned. Díaz joined the Dodgers this offseason on a three-year, $69 million deal to be the team's closer. He had a 10.50 ERA over six innings before going on the injured
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are giving Edwin Díaz one final chance to prove he belongs on the postseason roster.
On Friday, ahead of their series opener against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers have officially activated Díaz off the 15-day injured list. In order to make room on the active roster, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned.
Díaz joined the Dodgers this offseason on a three-year, $69 million deal to be the team's closer. He had a 10.50 ERA over six innings before going on the injured list and undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
Díaz made his long-awaited return in late July, and the Dodgers were hoping his early-season issues would be behind him.
Unfortunately, that wasn't the case.
The three-time All-Star had an even worse 12.91 ERA over 7.2 innings. He then went back on the IL — this time with a neck injury — and has been out for the last month.
Díaz struggled on his rehab assignment, and there were questions about whether the team would even give him another chance this season.
“He needs to pitch better. It hasn’t been good,” manager Dave Roberts said on Monday. “He’s going to pitch on Wednesday, and I guess we’ll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well."
He had a better rehab outing on Wednesday, pitching one scoreless inning. That was enough for the Dodgers to give him one more opportunity at the big league level.
It won't be as the team's closer, though.
What Will Edwin Diaz's Role Be For Dodgers?
The Dodgers will be using Díaz in low-leverage spots at first as they see if he can be an option for the postseason roster.
“I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Across Díaz's 16 appearances this season, he has a disastrous 11.85 ERA and four blown saves in 11 chances.
However, if he returns to form in time for the playoffs, all will be forgotten from his disappointing first season in LA.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts: “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”
El campocorto de los Dodgers coloca en perspectiva la participación de la novena en la postemporada por decimotercera vez en los últimos 14 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Cincinnati. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Reds de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Doc and the boys are ready for October. pic.twitter.com/krnwXYR7ap
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Freddie Freeman bringing back key from 2024 World Series to end slump
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Freddie Freeman has been mired in a lengthy slump, which can be partly attributed to a right knee tendinitis that sidelined him for back-to-back games last week. After going 0-for-8 in the Dodgers’ final two contests at loanDepot Park, Freeman bounced back with a three-hit performance in their series opener against the Cincinnati Reds. It was only his second multi-hit game of the month and first with three since Aug. 17. “I’ve been kind of working on this new thing in the cage these last couple
item.content:encoded:
Freddie Freeman has been mired in a lengthy slump, which can be partly attributed to a right knee tendinitis that sidelined him for back-to-back games last week.
After going 0-for-8 in the Dodgers’ final two contests at loanDepot Park, Freeman bounced back with a three-hit performance in their series opener against the Cincinnati Reds. It was only his second multi-hit game of the month and first with three since Aug. 17.
“I’ve been kind of working on this new thing in the cage these last couple days,” Freeman said on SportsNet LA. “Got to go for results-based things right now. I’ve got to get hot with two weeks to go. I’m looking to be hot for a few weeks. That’s all I’m trying to do.”
Freeman is exploring unorthodox ways to get back on track and recalled a key adjustment he made that led to his historic showing in the 2024 World Series.
“Just doing different work. I’m trying to find something that gets me results. We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here,” Freeman noted.
“Kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago, I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. (But) I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable. I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
Freeman followed his three-hit effort by going 0-for-5 in the Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Reds on Wednesday. He initially wasn’t expected to be in the lineup but showed enough encouraging signs that convinced Dodgers manager Dave Roberts to change course.
Freeman started again in the finale at Great American Ball Park and went 2-for-3 with an RBI as the Dodgers clinched the National League West division.
Dodgers managing Freddie Freeman’s right knee injury
With just over a week remaining in the regular season, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made it clear that the Dodgers are prioritizing the health of their players over anything else and will closely manage Freeman’s workload.
“I think it’s one of those things where we’ve got to manage it, and when I say that, it’s just pick spots to give him an off day here or there,” Roberts recently said. “Again, we’ve just got to make sure he’s at optimal health when we finish the season. So I think that he might not love it, but giving him a day off here or there might be beneficial.”

item.title: [heavy.com] Dodgers Provide Roki Sasaki Insight Ahead of Return From Injury
item.dc:creator: Toran Flores
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have faced multiple injury scares in the pitching rotation. Still, they remain focused on preparing for a third straight World Series win. One question about the Dodgers’ pitching centers on right-hander Roki Sasaki. The 24-year-old has been sidelined since revealing a blister on his throwing hand. He is eyeing a return before the postseason, although his role in Los Angeles’ rotation remains unknown. Learning of Blake Snell’s recent groin injury has forced the Dodgers to
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have faced multiple injury scares in the pitching rotation. Still, they remain focused on preparing for a third straight World Series win.
One question about the Dodgers’ pitching centers on right-hander Roki Sasaki. The 24-year-old has been sidelined since revealing a blister on his throwing hand. He is eyeing a return before the postseason, although his role in Los Angeles’ rotation remains unknown.
Learning of Blake Snell’s recent groin injury has forced the Dodgers to pivot to a new strategy.
“To be safe, the Dodgers are likely to keep building up Roki Sasaki as a starter,” wrote The Athletic’s Katie Woo. “Sasaki threw a four-inning simulated game Wednesday in Cincinnati. While the Dodgers would prefer to use Sasaki in relief in the postseason, keeping him stretched out on a starter’s workload is smart insurance as they await further developments with Snell.”
Roki Sasaki’s Success as a Postseason Relief Pitcher
While struggling in his first year with the Dodgers in 2025, the team moved Roki Sasaki to a relief role during the postseason. This change worked out well for Los Angeles on its path to a World Series win.
Through nine appearances during the 2025 postseason, Sasaki finished with a 0.84 ERA, 1.03 WHIP, three saves, and two holds. He allowed just one earned run across his postseason run.
Sasaki transitioned into 2026 with similar struggled as the year prior. In 23 starts this season, the second-year starter has a 5-5 record, 4.60 ERA, and 1.33 WHIP across 119.1 innings pitched.
Los Angeles is preparing to have a stacked postseason rotation. It includes 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, and Tyler Glasnow.
Dodgers Are Closing in on a First-Round Bye
With a little over a week left of the MLB regular season, the Dodgers have their eyes set on clinching a first-round bye in the postseason. Earlier this week, Los Angeles earned the NL West title.
Now, finishing as a top-two team in the National League will secure a top seed and a much-needed break before their postseason run. Entering Friday, the Dodgers hold a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed.
The top position in the NL is also very much on the table. The Milwaukee Brewers currently own the spot, but hold just a two-game lead over the Dodgers.
It will definitely be something to monitor heading into the weekend. Los Angeles faces the San Francisco Giants in two separate series and the San Diego Padres to finish out their regular season.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dave Roberts Addresses Josue De Paula's Spot on Dodgers Postseason Roster
item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown

With October right around the corner, all eyes are on LA to see if they will win three consecutive championships for the first time in MLB in a quarter-century. Superstar Shohei Ohtani has not been fully healthy essentially since the All-Star break, when he was scratched from not only his final start of the first half, but from all All-Star-related activities. After being shut down from p
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are under the biggest microscope in baseball as the regular season comes to a close. With October right around the corner, all eyes are on LA to see if they will win three consecutive championships for the first time in MLB in a quarter-century.
Superstar Shohei Ohtani has not been fully healthy essentially since the All-Star break, when he was scratched from not only his final start of the first half, but from all All-Star-related activities. After being shut down from pitching in early July, the concern has only grown coming out of an August where he only attained a .241 batting average for the month.
After Ohtani was placed on the injured list, Josue De Paula appeared to be the answer for the lack of Ohtani in the lineup.
Though it is obvious that De Paula will not be pitching, his offense has the potential to start to fill the enormous Ohtani-sized shoes. In Double-A, the 21-year-old slashed .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs and 104 RBIs, leading to a call-up that preceded any Triple-A action.
De Paula was hitless during the first two games of his MLB career, but earned his first hit via a towering fourth-inning home run last Sunday.
Due to his astounding minor league track record, his 92.6 mph exit velocity at the MLB level thus far, and the fact that the organization didn't feel the need for him to move up to Triple-A, there have been murmurs as to what his spot on a postseason roster may be.
Manager Dave Roberts spoke on if De Paula should be under consideration for a roster spot, even though he will have less than a month of MLB knowledge come October.
“Yeah, he should be [under consideration],” Roberts said. “This is more of a trial run, no promises. Just obviously having Shohei down and giving a guy that’s performed well an opportunity. Then you just sort of see where it takes us.
"I think right now that’s kind of where we’re at and take it day to day. I just hope he continues to perform and take those at-bats and then we’ll kind of see where we’re at in September.”
Roberts also clarified that the rookie's status for the postseason even being a potential storyline says more about the maturity and talent of De Paula.
“It’s been good that you can even bring that question up,” Roberts said. “But it’s still very early as far as however many at-bats or plate appearances he has taken. But in this small sample, yeah, it’s been good. But it’s certainly a much different level of focus with the postseason. But baseball is still baseball. I hope he makes our decision hard.”
Across seven games thus far, De Paula is 3-for-18 (.167) with one home run, four RBIs, seven walks and an OPS of .789.

Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.content:encoded:
Why Dodgers' top rookie of 2026 is not Josue De Paula originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers have no shortage of talent.
Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, the NL West club has one of, if not the best, rosters in the Majors.
Concerns about the bullpen are warranted. But a starting three in the rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, and one of Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and Justin Wrobleski is dominant.
With Ohtani on the IL, the Dodgers promoted a new talented prospect to replace him at designated hitter: slugger Josue De Paula.
De Paula promptly hit a homer just a few games into his first taste of the Majors and has a .789 OPS through 25 plate appearances.
But Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes it's too soon to label him the best Dodgers rookie of the season. Instead, Miller awarded that distinction to a middle infielder.
"There's already a case to be made for Josue De Paula in this spot, even though he just made his MLB debut as Shohei Ohtani's fill-in last Friday," Miller wrote.
"However, [Alex] Freeland spent much of the season as the Dodgers' primary second baseman, providing decent value with his glove while hitting just well enough to earn regular playing time."
Freeland doesn't have eye-popping offensive numbers, hitting .230 with four home runs and a 79 OPS+.
But he has +3 outs above average while playing at three infield spots, mainly second base.
De Paula could change Miller's mind during the final week of the regular season. Manager Dave Roberts should give him plenty of playing time.
For now, Freeland has done enough to warrant the title as the Dodgers' best rookie of the year.

item.title: [midiario.com] Dodgers convierten el Oeste en su territorio y celebran otro título de división
item.dc:creator: Luis Del Valle
item.description: Hay celebraciones que podrían convertirse en rutina, pero Los Angeles Dodgers se niegan a tratarlas como algo normal. La franquicia volvió a apoderarse del título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional al derrotar 8-2 a los Cincinnati Reds en el Great American Ball Park. Fue su quinto campeonato divisional consecutivo y el número 13 en las últimas 14 temporadas, otra cifra que dimensiona el dominio de Los Ángeles en esta etapa. King Tuck! pic.twitter.com/FGbgOZjXXS — Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodg
item.content:encoded:
Hay celebraciones que podrían convertirse en rutina, pero Los Angeles Dodgers se niegan a tratarlas como algo normal. La franquicia volvió a apoderarse del título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional al derrotar 8-2 a los Cincinnati Reds en el Great American Ball Park. Fue su quinto campeonato divisional consecutivo y el número 13 en las últimas 14 temporadas, otra cifra que dimensiona el dominio de Los Ángeles en esta etapa.
King Tuck! pic.twitter.com/FGbgOZjXXS
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Kyle Tucker prendió la fiesta
La ofensiva encontró en Kyle Tucker a su principal protagonista. El jardinero terminó de 4 hits en 5 turnos, conectó un jonrón y produjo tres carreras, quedándose a un triple de completar el ciclo.
i love kyle tucker pic.twitter.com/ePeIAxm7re
— 🌱 jaime (@dodgersrpf) September 17, 2026
Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula y Miguel Rojas también impulsaron carreras para unos Dodgers que no necesitaron de un abridor tradicional. Justin Wrobleski trabajó tres entradas perfectas para iniciar un partido manejado desde el bullpen.
El triunfo dejó a Los Ángeles con marca de 93-60, nueve juegos por encima de los Padres de San Diego, que también ganaron durante la jornada pero ya no tenían forma matemática de alcanzar el liderato divisional.
Un dominio que parece no terminar
La dimensión del logro va mucho más allá de 2026.
Los Dodgers han conquistado el Oeste 13 veces durante sus últimas 14 campañas. La única excepción ocurrió en 2021, cuando los San Francisco Giants terminaron por delante de ellos.
Además, desde que MLB instauró el sistema divisional en 1969, Los Ángeles encabeza las Grandes Ligas con 24 campeonatos de división.
La franquicia también alcanzó su decimocuarta clasificación consecutiva a la postemporada, igualando la histórica racha de Atlanta entre 1991 y 2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
Muncy todavía disfruta el champán
Pese a estar acostumbrado a estas celebraciones, Max Muncy dejó claro que el momento conserva su valor.
“Nunca lo doy por sentado”, aseguró el veterano durante la celebración, destacando lo especial que resulta poder festejar después de atravesar una temporada de 162 partidos.
Y esta vez hubo razones de sobra para descorchar las botellas. Los Dodgers ya habían asegurado días antes su presencia en octubre, pero conquistar la división les permitió completar otro de los grandes objetivos de la temporada regular.
Ahora viene lo que realmente quieren
El título del Oeste, sin embargo, no representa la meta definitiva.
Los Dodgers llegan a octubre como campeones consecutivos de las Series Mundiales de 2024 y 2025 y persiguen algo que ningún equipo consigue desde los Yankees de Nueva York de 1998, 1999 y 2000: levantar tres Clásicos de Otoño consecutivos.
La corona divisional confirma que la maquinaria sigue funcionando. Ahora el reto será convertir nuevamente ese dominio de seis meses en victorias durante octubre.

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Dodgers manager comments on future interest in Elly De La Cruz
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Abdón Ibarra
item.description: Elly De La Cruz is enjoying a career year in his fourth season with the Cincinnati Reds, and it included plenty of success against the Los Angeles Dodgers. That was an extension of De La Cruz’s career performance against the Dodgers, in which he’s hit .290 with seven home runs, 14 RBI and 17 runs scored in 26 career games. “He’s definitely had a lot of success against us,” manager Dave Roberts said on SportsNet LA when asked if felt as though De La Cruz was auditioning to become a Dodgers target
item.content:encoded:
Elly De La Cruz is enjoying a career year in his fourth season with the Cincinnati Reds, and it included plenty of success against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
That was an extension of De La Cruz’s career performance against the Dodgers, in which he’s hit .290 with seven home runs, 14 RBI and 17 runs scored in 26 career games.
“He’s definitely had a lot of success against us,” manager Dave Roberts said on SportsNet LA when asked if felt as though De La Cruz was auditioning to become a Dodgers target.
“I still recall that homer he hit off (Noah) Syndergaard here. I know him enough through All-Star Games and things like that, that he likes the big stage, he wants to play against the best and against us, he certainly performs. I think there’s a lot of willing takers for that person and talent.
“It’s nice to win games against those guys and still kind of be a fan and marvel at what he can do on a baseball field. He’s very impressive.”
In seven games against the Dodgers this season, De La Cruz batted .360/.407/1.040 with two doubles, five home runs and nine RBI.
De La Cruz’s talent should make him a foundational building block who is untouchable in trade talks, but the Reds do not have a great track record of success over the past 12 seasons. Their only two playoff appearances since 2014 were the 16-team playoff in 2020 and as the last National League Wild Card team in 2025 with an 83-79 record.
Cincinnati has yet to lock him De La Cruz long term, but that could change with his performance this year elevating him to the upper echelon of MLB’s hierarchy. For now, he has three years of arbitration remaining before becoming a free agent in 2030 as a soon-to-be 28-year-old.
Mookie Betts’ contract doesn’t expire until after the 2032 season, but that would not prevent the Dodgers from making a play for De La Cruz. Nor would the investment they made in 2024 by drafting Kellon Lindsey with their first pitck.
Elly De La Cruz previously impressed Dave Roberts
De La Cruz made MLB debut against the Dodgers back in 2023, going 1-for-2 with a double. Roberts had high praise for the blossoming star that season.
“He is as toolsy as any player in the big leagues,” Roberts said prior to that weekend series beginning. “The way he carried himself, the poise on the field, on a Major League field, so early in his career was remarkable. He’s a human highlight film. I like watching the highlights much more than in real-time, firsthand.
“But what a special talent. It’s good for the game of baseball.”

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers begin final homestand of the regular season hosting the Giants
item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo
item.description: The NL West crown has been secured, but the regular season grind carries on, with the next checkmark being a playoff bye, and if the Brewers stumble, maybe even the NL’s top record: the Dodgers open a series against the Giants, with the former looking like a near formality, four up on Atlanta with nine to go and threatening a Brewers team that’s only two games ahead after losing to the Pirates yesterday. Dodgers begin final homestand of the regular season hosting the Giants The Dodgers open a we
item.content:encoded:
The NL West crown has been secured, but the regular season grind carries on, with the next checkmark being a playoff bye, and if the Brewers stumble, maybe even the NL’s top record: the Dodgers open a series against the Giants, with the former looking like a near formality, four up on Atlanta with nine to go and threatening a Brewers team that’s only two games ahead after losing to the Pirates yesterday.
Dodgers begin final homestand of the regular season hosting the Giants
The Dodgers open a weekend set against a division rival they’ll face in six of their last nine games, the Giants
One might argue that more than specific and still important team accomplishments that the Dodgers may have between now and the end of the regular season, the key is to see individual players nearing their best form. For the purposes of this Friday game against the Giants, we’ll focus on Kyle Tucker and Tyler Glasnow, who fit the bill to a T of what we’re trying to discuss here.
Through his last eight games, Tucker isn’t just showing signs of life; he has been this team’s best hitter, securing 12 hits in just 29 at-bats and leaving the yard four times: the most home runs he has hit in such a short sample in the entire season. Outstanding during the road trip, Tucker has a chance to carry some momentum into the playoffs. At the same time, it’d be quite flat to see him reverse back into the hitter we’ve seen from most of the year as the team returns to Dodger Stadium, a place in which he carries a .572 OPS in 2026.
On the mound, it’ll be Tyler Glasnow, who, after returning from the IL with pristine control, walking just one batter in the first two starts back, has now walked seven in the last two, allowing a combined eight runs. Glasnow will be matched up against the offense with the lowest walk rate in baseball, the Giants at 7.5% BB%.
Tucker and Glasnow would be treated as the star players on most teams, but playing for the Dodgers, they serve slightly different roles even if the expectation for outstanding production is one and the same. Can Glasnow overcome his recent struggles while Tucker carries on in improved form? Standing in their way is the San Francisco Giants, a last-place club in everything but name, sitting in fourth place in the West with the second-worst record in the National League.
Friday game info
- Teams: Dodgers vs. Giants
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium
- Start time: 7:15 p.m.
- TV: Apple TV
- Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] Kyle Tucker’s flirtation with history gives Dodgers more hope of turnaround
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
